cases.description: Typical case – the underlying MMAIndicator reports a positive bar count (10). getBarCount() should return the same value.
Edge case – the underlying MMAIndicator reports zero bars. getBarCount() must forward this value unchanged.
Defensive case – if the underlying MMAIndicator (perhaps due to a bug) returns a negative bar count, getBarCount() should still return the exact value without modification.
Boundary case – the underlying MMAIndicator reports Integer.MAX_VALUE. getBarCount() must forward this maximum int value unchanged.
Boundary case – the underlying MMAIndicator reports Integer.MIN_VALUE. Even though this is an unlikely real‑world value, getBarCount() should return it verbatim.
Typical odd number – verifies that non‑even, non‑round numbers are propagated correctly.
Large positive number – ensures that getBarCount() works for high‑magnitude but still valid counts.
Negative value different from the already‑tested -5 – confirms that any negative integer is returned unchanged, highlighting the method's lack of validation.
When the ATRIndicator is constructed with a null averageTrueRangeIndicator, calling getBarCount() should throw a NullPointerException because the method dereferences the field.
If the underlying MMAIndicator's getBarCount() implementation throws a RuntimeException (e.g., IllegalStateException), getBarCount() must propagate that exception unchanged.
